title: Ledger is append-only and event-sourced
statement: The ledger accepts only appends of immutable events; no posting or balance can be updated or deleted, and balances are a fold of the event stream.
rationale: Market data can disappear and models can be retrained; the ledger cannot be reconstructed from guesses, so its history must be immutable.

verification.check: Re-folding the stored event stream from its first record equals stored balances; mutation: add an update path or skip an event in the fold and the refold test fails.

notes: The store is real and tested; the composition root is a stub whose doc comments describe steps (bind, consume) it does not perform.

title: Every ledger event balances per unit
statement: Each ledger event is double-entry: at least two positive postings whose debits equal credits exactly in every unit, refused otherwise (never plugged).
rationale: An unbalanced entry or a suspense plug hides an error the ledger exists to expose.

verification.check: Constructing or deserialising an unbalanced event is refused; mutation: remove the per-unit sum check and the refusal test fails.

notes: Type-level invariant; integrated wherever a LedgerEvent is built, including qip-ledgerd's store.

title: Ledger is multi-asset
statement: The ledger holds balances per account per unit for any asset (currencies, instruments, physical units), not a single currency.
rationale: A single-currency book cannot be authoritative for multi-asset positions.

verification.check: Postings in two units for one event are balanced independently and both balances are readable; mutation: key balances by account only and the test fails.

title: Ledger authoritative for cash and positions
statement: Cash and instrument positions are booked in the ledger from fills and the ledger, not a model or cache, is the authority for them.
rationale: The ledger is authoritative for this state; any other source is a guess (§15).

verification.check: The state is readable from ledger events after the producing event is applied; mutation: drop the posting and the balance check fails.

notes: Principle 6 ('two independent claims about the same fact will disagree') applies: kernel positions and ledger balances have no reconciliation.

title: Ledger authoritative for inventory
statement: Inventory (trading inventory and reservations against it) is held as ledger state.
rationale: The ledger is authoritative for this state; any other source is a guess (§15).

verification.check: The state is readable from ledger events after the producing event is applied; mutation: drop the posting and the balance check fails.

title: Ledger authoritative for obligations and commitments
statement: Obligations and commitments (e.g. unfunded private commitments, pending payables) are recorded as ledger state.
rationale: The ledger is authoritative for this state; any other source is a guess (§15).

verification.check: The state is readable from ledger events after the producing event is applied; mutation: drop the posting and the balance check fails.

title: Ledger records venue-reported fees
statement: Fees are booked in the ledger to a fees account equal to the venue-reported fee, and no fee is booked when the venue did not report one.
rationale: The ledger is authoritative for this state; any other source is a guess (§15).

verification.check: The state is readable from ledger events after the producing event is applied; mutation: drop the posting and the balance check fails.

title: Ledger tracks tax lots
statement: Tax lots are ledger state, so cost basis and holding period per lot are derivable from the ledger.
rationale: The ledger is authoritative for this state; any other source is a guess (§15).

verification.check: The state is readable from ledger events after the producing event is applied; mutation: drop the posting and the balance check fails.

title: Ledger tracks collateral and margin
statement: Collateral pledged and margin requirements are recorded as ledger state.
rationale: The ledger is authoritative for this state; any other source is a guess (§15).

verification.check: The state is readable from ledger events after the producing event is applied; mutation: drop the posting and the balance check fails.

title: Ledger records transfers
statement: Transfers of cash or assets between accounts, venues or regions are ledger events.
rationale: The ledger is authoritative for this state; any other source is a guess (§15).

verification.check: The state is readable from ledger events after the producing event is applied; mutation: drop the posting and the balance check fails.

title: Ledger records settlement state
statement: Each ledger event carries its settlement state through to settlement.
rationale: The ledger is authoritative for this state; any other source is a guess (§15).

verification.check: The state is readable from ledger events after the producing event is applied; mutation: drop the posting and the balance check fails.

notes: Live settlement is BLOCKED by ADR 0003; a simulated lifecycle is not.

title: Every posting cites the observed fact that caused it
statement: Ledger state is never inferred: every event names the cell, session, journal sequence/digest and order that produced it, and an event without a source is refused.
rationale: The ledger cannot be reconstructed from guesses; an unattributed posting cannot be reproduced.

verification.check: An event with an empty source field is refused; mutation: remove refuse_unnamed for the digest and the test fails.

title: Global journal with idempotent event IDs
statement: One global journal applies each event exactly once: redelivery of the same event ID changes nothing, and the same ID with different content is an integrity break.
rationale: Duplicated or replayed fills would double-book cash and positions.

verification.check: Any duplication/redelivery/crash sequence yields balances equal to one clean delivery; mutation: apply duplicates and the property fails.

title: Immutable lineage from intent to cash impact
statement: Each ledger event carries an immutable lineage intent -> order -> fill -> settlement -> position/cash impact that can be walked in both directions.
rationale: Without lineage, a cash movement cannot be explained back to the decision that caused it.

verification.check: Given a balance change, a reader recovers the order, journal entry and originating intent; mutation: drop order_id from SourceEvent and the walk fails.

title: Ledger has a trading subledger
statement: The ledger maintains a trading subledger whose postings roll up into the global double-entry journal.
rationale: Subledgers let each domain be reconciled independently while the global journal stays the single authority.

verification.check: A trading event posts to the trading subledger and the global trial balance still balances; mutation: route it elsewhere and the test fails.

title: Ledger has a treasury subledger
statement: The ledger maintains a treasury subledger whose postings roll up into the global double-entry journal.
rationale: Subledgers let each domain be reconciled independently while the global journal stays the single authority.

verification.check: A treasury event posts to the treasury subledger and the global trial balance still balances; mutation: route it elsewhere and the test fails.

title: Ledger has a custody subledger
statement: The ledger maintains a custody subledger whose postings roll up into the global double-entry journal.
rationale: Subledgers let each domain be reconciled independently while the global journal stays the single authority.

verification.check: A custody event posts to the custody subledger and the global trial balance still balances; mutation: route it elsewhere and the test fails.

title: Ledger has a physical inventory/commerce subledger
statement: The ledger maintains a physical inventory/commerce subledger whose postings roll up into the global double-entry journal.
rationale: Subledgers let each domain be reconciled independently while the global journal stays the single authority.

verification.check: A physical inventory/commerce event posts to the physical inventory/commerce subledger and the global trial balance still balances; mutation: route it elsewhere and the test fails.

title: Ledger has a fees/taxes subledger
statement: The ledger maintains a fees/taxes subledger whose postings roll up into the global double-entry journal.
rationale: Subledgers let each domain be reconciled independently while the global journal stays the single authority.

verification.check: A fees/taxes event posts to the fees/taxes subledger and the global trial balance still balances; mutation: route it elsewhere and the test fails.

title: Ledger has a private commitments subledger
statement: The ledger maintains a private commitments subledger whose postings roll up into the global double-entry journal.
rationale: Subledgers let each domain be reconciled independently while the global journal stays the single authority.

verification.check: A private commitments event posts to the private commitments subledger and the global trial balance still balances; mutation: route it elsewhere and the test fails.

title: Ledger has a user/mandate ownership subledger
statement: The ledger maintains a user/mandate ownership subledger whose postings roll up into the global double-entry journal.
rationale: Subledgers let each domain be reconciled independently while the global journal stays the single authority.

verification.check: A user/mandate ownership event posts to the user/mandate ownership subledger and the global trial balance still balances; mutation: route it elsewhere and the test fails.

title: Continuous external reconciliation with venues
statement: The ledger is continuously reconciled against venues' own records and every break is recorded and acted on.
rationale: An internal ledger never checked against the counterparty's record can drift silently.

verification.check: A seeded difference between ledger and venues record produces a recorded break; mutation: disable the comparison and no break is recorded.

title: Continuous external reconciliation with banks
statement: The ledger is continuously reconciled against banks' own records and every break is recorded and acted on.
rationale: An internal ledger never checked against the counterparty's record can drift silently.

verification.check: A seeded difference between ledger and banks record produces a recorded break; mutation: disable the comparison and no break is recorded.

title: Continuous external reconciliation with custodians
statement: The ledger is continuously reconciled against custodians' own records and every break is recorded and acted on.
rationale: An internal ledger never checked against the counterparty's record can drift silently.

verification.check: A seeded difference between ledger and custodians record produces a recorded break; mutation: disable the comparison and no break is recorded.

title: Continuous external reconciliation with wallets
statement: The ledger is continuously reconciled against wallets' own records and every break is recorded and acted on.
rationale: An internal ledger never checked against the counterparty's record can drift silently.

verification.check: A seeded difference between ledger and wallets record produces a recorded break; mutation: disable the comparison and no break is recorded.

title: Continuous external reconciliation with warehouses/marketplaces
statement: The ledger is continuously reconciled against warehouses/marketplaces' own records and every break is recorded and acted on.
rationale: An internal ledger never checked against the counterparty's record can drift silently.

verification.check: A seeded difference between ledger and warehouses/marketplaces record produces a recorded break; mutation: disable the comparison and no break is recorded.

title: Continuous external reconciliation with settlement agents
statement: The ledger is continuously reconciled against settlement agents' own records and every break is recorded and acted on.
rationale: An internal ledger never checked against the counterparty's record can drift silently.

verification.check: A seeded difference between ledger and settlement agents record produces a recorded break; mutation: disable the comparison and no break is recorded.

title: Decisions store their version identifiers
statement: Every model, strategy, capital and risk decision records the version identifiers (model, strategy plan, policy/grant, risk limits) in force, so it can be explained and replayed.
rationale: A decision whose versions are unknown cannot be replayed or explained.

verification.check: Replaying a journal reconstructs which policy/plan/model versions governed each order; mutation: drop the PolicyApplied record and replay cannot name the version.

title: Reflex node never waits on the global brain
statement: A regional reflex node takes every hot-path decision from its local package and state without waiting on the global brain or any central call.
rationale: A cell that blocks on the centre turns a partition into an outage and adds round-trip latency to every decision.

verification.check: With the centre unreachable, the node runs the same passes and sends the same orders; mutation: make the pass call the mesh and the test hangs or diverges.

notes: Passes are driven by health-probe connections, not a scheduler (main.rs:878-1003; scheduler.rs is a 2-line stub).

title: Reflex node runs a signed package
statement: The node runs a signed package containing models, strategies, beliefs, feasibility rules, capital grants, risk limits, target inventory and opportunity definitions, verified before use and combined with live local state.
rationale: An unsigned or partially verified package lets anyone who can reach the node change what it trades.

verification.check: A payload with a bad signature or wrong cell is refused and changes nothing; each slot is consumed by the cell; mutation: skip verification and the refusal test fails.

title: Node embeds a non-blocking fabric client
statement: Each reflex node embeds a non-blocking Rust event-fabric client that forwards to the regional fabric.
rationale: Without a client the node's outcomes never reach the durable fabric.

verification.check: The deployed node writes journal records to a spool and a drain ships them to qip-fabricd; mutation: remove the mirror and no record arrives.

title: Node keeps a local append-only event journal
statement: Each reflex node keeps a local append-only, hash-chained event journal of every decision and refusal.
rationale: The journal is the only account of what a cell decided alone.

verification.check: Entries chain by digest; a tampered or dropped entry breaks verification; mutation: skip chaining and the chain test fails.

notes: Bounded-retention rule: the deployed node keeps every entry in memory for the session (journal.rs default retention).

title: Decision thread never waits on the fabric
statement: The decision thread writes to preallocated bounded lock-free queues/journals and continues; it never blocks on the fabric or disk.
rationale: A decision loop that blocks on a disk or broker inherits that system's latency and outages.

verification.check: With the writer stalled, ship returns immediately and entries stay unshipped; mutation: use a blocking send and the test times out.

title: Outcomes, telemetry and acks drained asynchronously
statement: Durable outcomes, telemetry and policy/model acknowledgments are drained asynchronously from the node to the regional fabric.
rationale: Synchronous draining couples the hot path to fabric health.

verification.check: Outcome and ack records appear on the fabric after the pass returns; mutation: drop the drain and none arrive.

title: Latency-sensitive cross-region arbitrage is direct peer-to-peer
statement: Truly latency-sensitive cross-region arbitrage coordination travels as direct peer-to-peer Reflex Mesh traffic, not via the broker-mediated fabric.
rationale: Broker mediation adds hops and couples coordination to durable-log health.

verification.check: Peer messages are sent node-to-node over the mesh transport; mutation: route them through qip-fabricd and the placement test fails.

title: Native venue feed adapters with normalization
statement: Feed adapters consume native venue feeds and normalise them into the platform's market message form.
rationale: Without native adapters the cell trades only what a simulator shows it.

verification.check: Captured native bytes decode into normalised book events applied by the cell; mutation: break a decoder field and the decode test fails.

title: Sequence and gap detection with timestamping
statement: Feed handling detects sequence gaps, marks the affected book stale until resynchronised, and timestamps every message.
rationale: A price from before a gap reaching an order is a trade on a book that no longer exists.

verification.check: A skipped sequence marks the book stale and no order is priced from it until resync; mutation: ignore the gap event and an order is sent.

notes: COMPLETE as code behaviour on the simulated feed path; not deployed.

title: Local books and state
statement: The node holds local order books, trades, funding, borrow, venue health, inventory and reservations.
rationale: Every local decision must read local state, not ask the centre.

verification.check: Each state element updates from its input and is read by the pass; mutation: stop updating venue health and quarantine never fires.

title: Incremental bounded-cost feature engine
statement: Features are computed incrementally (dirty-marking on ingest) at a bounded cost per message.
rationale: Recomputing every feature on every tick makes latency proportional to feature count.

verification.check: Ingesting one message recomputes only dependants; mutation: mark everything dirty and the recompute-count test fails.

title: Tiny local models with calibrated scores
statement: Reflex inference runs tiny local models producing calibrated scores, only models promoted by the centre.
rationale: An unpromoted or uncalibrated model trading at the edge is unreviewed risk.

verification.check: A plan's inline model runs only when the manifest names it at its digest, and its score is calibrated; mutation: skip the manifest check and the refusal test fails.

title: Compiled strategy runtime and opportunity detectors
statement: The node runs compiled strategy predicates and opportunity detectors from the signed plan.
rationale: Interpreting unreviewed strategy code at the edge is unbounded risk.

verification.check: A plan named by digest compiles and its signals reach the pass; mutation: a digest mismatch deploys nothing.

title: Arbitrage scanner over whitelisted and discovered cycles
statement: The node's arbitrage scanner evaluates whitelisted and discovered graph cycles, for both local and distributed opportunities.
rationale: A scanner limited to a fixed list misses new cycles; one with no list trades unreviewed paths.

verification.check: A whitelisted triangle with dislocated books becomes an opportunity; a discovered cycle outside the whitelist is reported; mutation: drop the whitelist edges and no opportunity is found.

title: Cross-strategy intent netting and internal crossing
statement: Intents from different strategies are netted and opposing interest is crossed internally before reaching a venue, with attribution preserved.
rationale: Sending both sides of offsetting intents pays two spreads and two fees for no exposure change.

verification.check: Two opposing intents within the window cross at the mid and move both lots; mutation: disable cross_internally and both reach the venue.

title: Local risk and feasibility gate
statement: Before an order exists, a local deterministic gate enforces hard constraints, capacity, inventory, limits and expected edge after costs.
rationale: A limit checked after the order exists is a report, not a control.

verification.check: An infeasible intent never reaches the venue adapter; mutation: bypass the gate and the no-order test fails.

title: Router with order types, venue selection, leg sequencing, quoting, cancel/replace
statement: The node's router supports order types, venue selection, leg sequencing, a quote engine and cancel/replace.
rationale: Without these the cell can only send one shape of order to one place.

verification.check: Each function is exercised through Cell::work and a pass; mutation: remove requote and the cancel/replace test fails.

title: Peer mesh client for summaries, tokens, reservations, sagas
statement: The node's peer mesh client exchanges fast state summaries, opportunity tokens, reservations and saga messages with peers.
rationale: Distributed cycles cannot be coordinated without a peer client.

verification.check: Two nodes exchange token, reserved, fire, fill and unwind messages over a transport; mutation: drop a message kind and the protocol test fails.

title: Journal forwarded to ledger and learning asynchronously
statement: The node's durable local event stream is forwarded asynchronously to the ledger and to learning.
rationale: Fills that never reach the ledger are trades nobody booked.

verification.check: A fill journaled at the node is booked by qip-ledgerd; mutation: drop the forward and the balance does not move.

title: Reflex Mesh and Event & Control Fabric are separate
statement: Mesh messages (short-lived, latency-sensitive peer state) and fabric messages (durable, replayable control, journal and outcome records) travel on separate paths.
rationale: Mixing them makes coordination latency depend on durable-log health, and durable records depend on ephemeral peers.

verification.check: Peer message kinds cannot carry durable pack/policy/grant records and vice versa; mutation: decode a policy from a peer frame and the refusal test fails.

title: Fabric outage does not stall local decisions
statement: A fabric (or central plane) outage never stalls a live local decision.
rationale: A cell that stops when the fabric stops turns a broker outage into a trading outage.

verification.check: With the store/fabric failing, passes continue and orders are still decided; mutation: return the flush error from the loop and the node stops.

title: Mesh outage does not prevent journaling or control distribution
statement: A Reflex Mesh (peer) outage never prevents durable journaling or control/policy distribution.
rationale: Coupling durability to peer health loses the record exactly when coordination fails.

verification.check: With peers unreachable, the journal still ships and policies still apply; mutation: gate flush on mesh health and the test fails.

title: No remote dependency on a local hot-path decision
statement: No remote dependency (centre or peer) is required for a local hot-path decision; peers may exchange latency-sensitive state but the local decision never waits on it.
rationale: The corrected v12 rule: physics forbids a round trip on the reflex path.

verification.check: qip-edge's hot path (on_bytes, work) performs no I/O and qip-edge does not depend on a socket-owning crate in those paths; mutation: add a transport call in work and the architecture test fails.

title: Distant legs handled with prepositioning, epochs, TTLs, sagas
statement: Cross-region cycles use pre-positioned capital/inventory, synchronized opportunity epochs, bounded TTLs and saga-style recovery instead of assuming distant legs are atomic.
rationale: Treating distant legs as atomic strands a leg when another fails.

verification.check: An epoch without TTL or unwind policy is refused; nothing fires after expiry; recovery loss is bounded; mutation: allow ttl=0 and the refusal test fails.

title: Graph node identity includes representation, settlement stage and region
statement: Each arbitrage graph node is (asset, venue, representation, settlement stage, region).
rationale: Two holdings of the same asset at different settlement stages or regions are not interchangeable; collapsing them prices impossible conversions.

verification.check: Two nodes differing only in settlement stage or region are distinct and no zero-cost edge joins them; mutation: drop region from the key and the test fails.

title: Edges carry rate, fees and size-dependent slippage
statement: Each conversion edge carries price/rate, fees and size-dependent slippage, and the cycle is priced by walking real depth at size.
rationale: A spread that omits a cost is theoretical, not executable (§17.1).

verification.check: The net edge falls by exactly the named cost when it is introduced; mutation: omit the deduction and the hand-computed net differs.

notes: §17.1's ten edge attributes are grouped into four requirements.

title: Edges carry carry/funding and borrow cost
statement: Each edge's net value includes carry/funding and borrow cost over the time capital is committed.
rationale: A spread that omits a cost is theoretical, not executable (§17.1).

verification.check: The net edge falls by exactly the named cost when it is introduced; mutation: omit the deduction and the hand-computed net differs.

notes: §17.1's ten edge attributes are grouped into four requirements.

title: Edges carry transfer/bridge/logistics cost and tax/duty
statement: Each edge includes transfer, bridge or logistics cost and a tax/duty estimate where applicable.
rationale: A spread that omits a cost is theoretical, not executable (§17.1).

verification.check: The net edge falls by exactly the named cost when it is introduced; mutation: omit the deduction and the hand-computed net differs.

notes: §17.1's ten edge attributes are grouped into four requirements.

title: Edges carry settlement risk, fill probability and time
statement: Each edge includes settlement risk, probability of fill and time.
rationale: A spread that omits a cost is theoretical, not executable (§17.1).

verification.check: The net edge falls by exactly the named cost when it is introduced; mutation: omit the deduction and the hand-computed net differs.

notes: §17.1's ten edge attributes are grouped into four requirements.

title: Cycles of 2-20 legs evaluated for executable expected value
statement: Cycles of 2 to 20 legs are evaluated for executable expected value after all costs, not theoretical spread; longer or shorter cycles are refused.
rationale: A spread on mid prices that does not survive the book is the default failure of arbitrage systems.

verification.check: A 21-leg cycle and a configured maximum are refused naming the limit; a cycle profitable on mids but not at size is refused; mutation: widen MAX_CYCLE_EDGES and the leg-limit test fails.

title: Global arbitrage brain discovers templates and prepositions capital
statement: A global/warm arbitrage brain continuously discovers candidate cycle templates and prepositions inventory/capital for them.
rationale: Distant cycles cannot be executed in time unless capital and inventory are already in place.

verification.check: The centre publishes a cycle whitelist from discovery and capital grants/inventory targets for the regions it names; mutation: stop discovery and the whitelist is empty.

title: Nodes publish compressed executable edge states
statement: Reflex nodes publish compressed executable edge states, not raw books, to peers or regional coordinators.
rationale: Shipping raw books across regions is too slow and too large for coordination.

verification.check: A node emits a bounded edge-state summary per edge; mutation: send the raw book and the size bound fails.

title: Opportunity epoch names cycle, legs, size, edge, versions, TTL, unwind
statement: An opportunity epoch identifies the cycle, legs, size, minimum edge, model versions, TTL and unwind policy, and an epoch missing any is refused.
rationale: A token with no unwind policy is a cycle with no loss bound.

verification.check: An epoch missing any of the seven fields is refused naming it; mutation: default a missing field and the test fails.

title: Local feasibility then atomic in-region reservation
statement: Each participating node runs local feasibility and then reserves the required inventory/capital atomically inside its region before declaring readiness.
rationale: Reserving before the gate holds capital for a leg that will never be sent.

verification.check: A gate refusal reserves nothing and the decline reaches the coordinator; a book that cannot hold every leg holds none; mutation: reserve before gating and the test fails.

title: FIRE only when the reservation condition is met
statement: The coordinator or deterministic rule declares FIRE only when the configured reservation condition is met, and no leg precedes FIRE.
rationale: Firing on partial reservations strands legs.

verification.check: FIRE is declared exactly when every leg is reserved; an unmet condition within TTL is rejected by name and sends no leg; mutation: fire on one missing reservation and the test fails.

title: Legs execute concurrently or risk-ordered per cycle policy
statement: After FIRE, legs execute concurrently or in risk-ordered sequence according to the cycle's policy.
rationale: Sending the most reversible leg first leaves the irreversible one exposed.

verification.check: A policy selecting risk order sends the least reversible leg first; a concurrent policy sends all; mutation: reverse order and the plan test fails.

title: Partial fills drive resize, hedge, reroute or unwind
statement: Fills are streamed peer-to-peer and a partial fill triggers a resize, hedge, reroute or unwind state transition.
rationale: A cycle that ignores a short fill carries the unmatched remainder as unhedged exposure.

verification.check: A first leg filling 75% sends later legs at 75%; under the minimum viable fraction no further leg is sent; mutation: ignore the fill fraction and the decomposition test fails.

title: Cycle completion recorded to the global ledger
statement: Cycle completion is recorded to the global ledger.
rationale: A completed cycle absent from the ledger is unbooked P&L.

verification.check: Every filled leg of a completed cycle appears as a balanced ledger event; mutation: drop one leg's posting and the cycle's cash does not net.

title: Inventory drift becomes a rebalancing task
statement: Inventory drift after a cycle becomes a treasury/capital rebalancing task.
rationale: Drift left unaddressed slowly removes the prepositioned inventory future cycles depend on.

verification.check: Drift beyond tolerance yields one task per place citing the epoch; mutation: ignore tolerance and the test fails.

title: Failed, declined and partial cycles counterfactually scored
statement: Every failed, declined or partial cycle is counterfactually scored to learn whether the coordination rule was too conservative.
rationale: Without counterfactuals the system cannot tell caution from correctness.

verification.check: A declined cycle is marked against later prices and the scored result is recorded; mutation: skip declined cycles and no score is produced.

title: Coordination latency, leg risk and unwind cost priced in
statement: The opportunity's value is net of coordination latency, leg risk and unwind cost.
rationale: A distant multi-leg cycle priced as atomic overstates its edge.

verification.check: Raising coordination latency or unwind cost lowers net edge until the cycle is refused; mutation: zero the latency deduction and the test fails.

title: Cycles without achievable guarantees are rejected
statement: When required guarantees cannot be achieved, the cycle is rejected, never treated as riskless arbitrage.
rationale: Treating a non-atomic cycle as riskless is how a strand becomes a loss.

verification.check: A cycle whose loss bound cannot be established is rejected by name and sends no leg; mutation: allow fire without the bound and the test fails.

title: Common venue capability contract retaining native features
statement: Venue adapters expose a common capability contract while retaining venue-native features.
rationale: A lowest-common-denominator adapter loses the features that make a venue worth using.

verification.check: Each adapter implements the common trait and exposes its native extension; mutation: remove an extension and the venue's native test fails.

title: Execution modes only where legally and operationally supported
statement: Order taking, market making, liquidity provision, cross-venue routing, derivatives, event contracts, decentralized venues and physical marketplaces are each enabled per venue only where legally and operationally supported.
rationale: An execution mode enabled without legal and operational support is an unlicensed activity.

verification.check: A mode not recorded as supported is refused at send; mutation: enable all modes by default and the refusal test fails.

notes: 'paper' is recorded as the jurisdiction for the two enabled modes.

title: Dynamic fair value, spread, skew and size
statement: Market-making quotes derive fair value, spread, skew and size from volatility, inventory, queue value, adverse selection and confidence.
rationale: Static quotes are picked off when volatility or toxicity rises.

verification.check: Each input moves its component in the stated direction; mutation: ignore inventory and the skew test fails.

notes: Deliberately structurally unable to submit (acceptance test asserts it).

title: Portfolio-aware quoting
statement: Hedges and correlated exposure affect quote size before a fill occurs.
rationale: Quoting each instrument in isolation accumulates correlated exposure.

verification.check: Correlated exposure in the inputs shrinks quote size; mutation: ignore it and the test fails.

title: Quote-rate and message-ratio controls
statement: Per-venue quote-rate and message-to-trade ratio limits refuse messages before the gateway is called.
rationale: Breaching a venue's message limits gets the participant throttled or expelled.

verification.check: Quotes past a venue's rate or below its trade ratio are refused before the gateway; mutation: skip the budget and the gateway is called.

title: Cancel/replace budgets
statement: Cancels and replaces are charged against a budget with a reserve kept for mass cancel.
rationale: A requote storm that exhausts the budget leaves nothing to withdraw orders on a halt.

verification.check: A requote the budget cannot fund whole withdraws nothing; a requote is refused rather than funded from the mass-cancel reserve; mutation: charge one message and the test fails.

title: Venue-specific microstructure models
statement: Quoting uses venue-specific microstructure models.
rationale: One model for every venue misprices queue and toxicity at most of them.

verification.check: Two venues with different policies produce different quotes for the same inputs; mutation: return the default policy for all and the test fails.

title: Market making and arbitrage share one reservation fabric
statement: Capital and inventory used by market making and arbitrage are reserved through one reservation fabric so neither can spend what the other holds.
rationale: Two reservation books over one capital pool each pass a check the other has already spent.

verification.check: A quote and an arbitrage leg drawing on the same capital cannot both reserve it; mutation: give quoting a separate ledger and both pass.

title: Market creation is a governed workflow
statement: Market creation, listing or seeding happens only through a governed product workflow with recorded venue, product and jurisdiction approval; no model action may create one.
rationale: An unrestricted model creating markets is an unlicensed product launch.

verification.check: An admission cannot be obtained without all three recorded permissions nor built/decoded elsewhere; mutation: admit with two and the test fails.

title: Market factory creates, lists, seeds and prices markets
statement: Where venue and jurisdiction allow, the platform can create/list a market or instrument, seed initial liquidity, publish pricing rules and manage its inventory.
rationale: Stated as an obligation in the source without a named failure.

verification.check: An approved creation lists an instrument at the simulated venue, seeds resting liquidity and publishes its pricing rule; mutation: make seed a no-op and the venue shows no liquidity.
